text:
We read a Tokyo hotel's own floor plans for two people with two big suitcases. The ¥15,250 double was 13.8 m². A flat one area farther out was 25 m² for ¥10,968 👇

🎯 Bet you can't guess the cheapest option. See if you're right 👉 https://japanbystation.com/tokyo-double-or-twin-two-suitcases

Our sample night: Wednesday 16 December 2026, 2 adults, Booking.com prices including taxes.

🛏️ THE DOUBLE

1️⃣ ICI HOTEL Ueno Shin Okachimachi, 3 minutes from Shin-Okachimachi Station. The double was ¥15,250.

📐 The hotel's plan shows 13.80 m², a 140 cm bed against one wall and one strip of floor roughly 85–90 cm wide beside it. One case opens there. The second goes on the bed.

🛏️ THE TWIN

2️⃣ Same hotel, 18.40 m², ¥19,650. That is ¥4,400 more for 4.6 m² more.

📐 But the plan draws the two 120 cm beds side by side with almost no gap, so the second bed takes most of the extra space.

🏠 BIGGER, ONE AREA OUT

3️⃣ A 25 m² flat at Brillia ist Kinshi Park, 5 minutes from Kinshicho Station: ¥10,968.

🚇 From Kinshicho, Shinjuku was 21 minutes and Shibuya 31 minutes on our Wednesday morning. From the Ueno hotel: 27 and 33.

⚠️ The catch: no staffed desk, check-in 16:00–22:00 only.

✅ OUR TAKE

For two big cases, we'd take the bigger room farther out. If your days are around Ueno and Asakusa, or you land in the morning, the Ueno hotel makes more sense. There, its 18 m² deluxe double at ¥18,750 was a better upgrade than the twin.
